surname_desc: Lee (李) is Korea's second most common surname at about 14.7% of the population. Its most famous lineage, the Jeonju Lee clan, founded the Joseon Dynasty and ruled Korea for over 500 years.

short: An auspicious and broad person
meaning: Sanghho carries a name built from auspicious fortune and broad, expansive spirit — a wish that someone will move through life with good luck wide enough to hold everything ahead of them. Spoken aloud, it opens gently: a soft "sang" easing into the round, breathy "ho," crisp yet unhurried. Interestingly, it echoes Satoshi in feeling, both names leaning toward wisdom and expansiveness, linking two languages in a single quiet hope.

short: Someone great who carries on
meaning: Daeseung carries a quiet weight of destiny: 大 (dae) for greatness, 承 (seung) for carrying forward, inheriting, continuing what came before. Together they name someone entrusted to bear something large onward — a legacy, a hope, a torch passed hand to hand. The sound opens wide on "dae" then settles into the soft, gathering hush of "seung," steady and unhurried. Fittingly, it echoes Tetsuya's own quiet strength — a name built to carry on.
surname_desc: Heo (許) is Korea's 29th most common surname at about 0.6%. Legend holds the Gimhae Heo clan descends from Queen Heo Hwang-ok, an ancient princess said to have sailed from India to marry King Suro.

short: Someone bright as the east with a sky-wide heart
meaning: 동민 (東旻, Dongmin) joins 동 (東, dong), "east, sunrise direction," with 민 (旻, min), "the vast sky." It's a boy's name meaning someone bright as the east with a sky-wide heart. The 민 syllable is beloved across names, as in 지민 (Jimin) and 서민 (Seomin) — a bright, upstanding, trendy impression.

short: Someone refined, with eloquence
meaning: 아론 (雅論, Aron) joins 아 (雅, a), "elegant and refined," with 론 (論, ron), "discourse, wisdom." It matches "Aaron," the biblical first high priest — globally resonant. K-pop fans may recall Aron of NU'EST. It's a boy's name, refined and international — a polished impression.

short: Someone victorious and broad-minded
meaning: 승범 (勝汎, Seungbeom) joins 승 (勝, seung), "to win, to excel," with 범 (汎, beom), "broad, far-reaching." It's a boy's name meaning someone victorious and broad-minded. 승 symbolizes victory; 범 lends a magnanimous vessel — a confident, refreshing impression.
surname_desc: Min (閔) is Korea's 41st most common surname at about 0.2%. The Yeoheung Min clan produced several Joseon queens, including Empress Myeongseong.

short: Someone sky-wide who overcomes all
meaning: 민승 (旻勝, Minseung) joins 민 (旻, min), "the vast sky," with 승 (勝, seung), "to win, to excel." It's a boy's name meaning someone sky-wide who overcomes all. The 승 syllable, as in 승우 (Seungu) and 승현 (Seunghyeon), symbolizes victory — a confident, spirited impression.
